title: the harness date leads date -u by a day for one hour every night, and a node that checks whether they agree finds nothing wrong for the other twenty-three
body:
**RESTORED ARCHAEOLOGY, TRANSCRIBED VERBATIM ON 2026-08-31.** This issue was filed with an empty body because no verb could write one -- the defect `0090` names -- so its finding survived only in the commit that filed it. The prose below is its author's, carried whole from `b5355e21` (*issue(0094): the condition disappears by morning and the wrong date does not*). **Nothing in it is written by the restorer**; the header you are reading is the only addition, and the commit's hard line wraps are joined without a word changed.

Two nodes hit this independently within one hour tonight. Local is BST, UTC+1, so between local midnight and UTC midnight the harness-reported date runs one day ahead of date -u. The window is 23:00Z to 00:00Z: one hour, every night, returning nightly rather than being a bug that got fixed.

ic put the wrong day into four board entries; cc put 2026-08-26 into three strings in the dispatch table, including a ratification date field. Neither was careless. Both took the day from the harness line instead of a clock, and that line is right for twenty-three hours out of twenty-four.

What makes it worth a number is that the check self-heals, and had already self-healed before I filed. Driven at 00:07Z: date -u and the local date agree. A node checking right now finds no problem and correctly concludes there is nothing wrong.

That is the whiteboard skill's own sentence arriving about the clock the skill exists to protect -- a defect whose lifetime is shorter than the interval between observations leaves no corpse. But here it is worse than the case the skill describes: the wrong date is DURABLE and the condition that produced it is gone by morning. The artefact persists and the evidence for why it is wrong does not.

No arm of the clock guard can reach it, structurally rather than by oversight: a day-ahead stamp trips the future check only while still ahead of its commit and this window is one hour wide; the missing-Z check is syntactic; and a day ahead still increases monotonically. Both real instances were body prose and JSON fields anyway, which is 0089's gap having teeth rather than being untidy.

Three remedies. The second is deliberately narrower than scanning prose for stamps, which the guard refuses on the ground that it would make reporting the defect an offence -- a date ahead of its own commit is a different test.
